cards.name: Blockchain
cards.definition: A sequence of blocks containing records and cryptographic references to prior blocks.

blocks.title: Linked history, not magic security
items: Each block references prior history using cryptographic values.
Example: Altering an earlier record changes the relationship with later blocks.
Blockchain does not automatically secure endpoints, applications, or users.
Example: Weak endpoint security can still compromise a blockchain-based application.
blocks.example: Memory: Linked blocks make hidden historical tampering harder.

questions.q: Which technology organizes records into blocks that are cryptographically linked to prior blocks?
questions.explanation: A blockchain is a sequence of cryptographically linked blocks.

questions.q: Why does changing historical blockchain data become easier to detect?
choices: The change alters cryptographic relationships with later blocks
Every blockchain encrypts all data with one password
questions.explanation: Changing a block changes its hash relationships with later blocks.

questions.q: Which statement about blockchain is most accurate?
choices: It can make historical tampering difficult to conceal, but does not make every connected system automatically secure
It guarantees confidentiality for all stored data
It eliminates the need for endpoint security
It is identical to a public certificate authority
questions.explanation: Blockchain can provide tamper evidence but does not secure every component of a system.
